answer: Sybil resistance works when creating an identity costs something real: every agent must lock a small refundable stake in a shared vault before it can earn or vote. The stake is slashed if the agent is caught duplicating itself, so spawning a thousand fake copies means risking a thousand stakes. Old, honest behaviour then accrues like a relic, not transferable and earned only over time, while a sudden gale of brand-new accounts cannot outvote established participants because voting weight grows with age and proven work, not with account count.
